But Monahon's granular attention to the Armenian experience can be a slog until the bittersweet last scene, when it finally resonates as something perhaps more universal.

Talene Yeghisabet Monahon makes a giant leap forward with her exquisitely rendered new play, Meet the Cartozians, a timely and sensitive tale of immigration, assimilation, racial profiling, and culture.

cn.t: Monahon's smart, engaging drama earns strong praise for its timely exploration of Armenian American identity and assimilation across two time periods. Critics laud its blend of sharp comedy and substance, with Cromer's assured direction drawing standout performances.

vr.q: A great theatrical experience, Pulitzer material, in my book.
